column1: # planning/fidelity/harnesses.pairing.tsv — which build node answers which mock affordance.
# Four tab-separated columns:  state <TAB> affordance <TAB> node <TAB> citation
# This file declares ONLY the pairing. It never declares a status: present, divergent, absent and
# unclassified are computed by scripts/acceptance/mock_fidelity.py from the two artifacts on every
# run, which is what makes `present` earned by measuring rather than asserted. Deleting a line here
# does not delete a row from the ledger — the mock side is derived from the mock on every run, so an
# affordance with no line becomes `absent`, which is a finding.
# A citation is external and PRE-EXISTING: a file and the claim it already makes, or a measurement
# and the day it was taken. A justification composed while filling this in is motivated
# EVERY CITATION OPENS WITH `Dn · `, naming the divergence in harnesses.layers.json this row's
# finding falls under. A row whose citation carries no number, or a number that file does not
#   node = -            the affordance has no counterpart in the build
# THE ONE STRUCTURAL FACT that decides most of this file: the mock draws six harness cards with
# hand-written contents, and the build draws one card per row the route returned. So a mock
# affordance inside a card pairs with the SAME affordance inside the card for the same harness, and
# the two lists are the same length only because the fixture carries the same six harnesses in the
# same order — which is deliberate (HarnessFixtures.populated) rather than a coincidence to rely on.
